summary: Rapid 5xx elevation from concurrent long-lived streams and bulk embedding fanout on customer's dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth (dedicated pool) reported a sharp rise in 5xx responses impacting both chat streaming and embedding upload endpoints. Error rate rose from baseline ~0.4% to ~12% over an 18-minute window starting 2026-03-14T09:12:00Z. Impacted tenants saw streaming disconnects and ~50% of large embedding uploads failing with 502/503/504 variants.

Impact:
- Customer reported degraded UX for interactive chat and failed background embedding jobs.
- Estimated 30% of requests for this tenant returned 5xx during the peak.
- No invoice/billing discrepancies reported.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool: cluster-dedicated-usw-06 (prod-us-west)
- Ingress: api-gateway (v2.7.1) fronting tenant routes
- Serving runtime: redwood-runtime 1.13.0 (nvml 520.61)
- Observed on model variants: openchat-v2-large (fp16) and embed-small-quant (int8)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer runs interactive sessions (long-lived streaming) while concurrently uploading large embedding batches (multipart uploads, 10k vectors).
2) After ~10 minutes of sustained mixed load, api-gateway accept-queue length grows and hedged retries increase.
3) Serving runtimes start to exhibit GPU driver NVML resets on a subset of workers, followed by runtime worker restarts and KV cache thrashing.
4) Requests routed to affected hosts return 502/503/504. Canary route weights shifted (see investigation) causing traffic to concentrate on warm-but-fragmented instances.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- api-gateway: accept_queue_length: 0 -> 420 in 12m; open_fds trending up; 5xx_rate: 0.4% -> 11.7%
- runtime kube events: "nvml: GPU driver reset" on nodes gw-rt-07, gw-rt-09 at 2026-03-14T09:25:42Z
- runtime logs: repeated OOM watcher restarts followed by watchdog kill: "runtime: fatal: nvml reset observed, initiating restart"
- kvcache: eviction_rate spike 6x, cold-prefetch latency 220ms -> 1.9s

Initial hypothesis:
- Mixed workload (long-lived streaming + large embedding multipart uploads) caused connection and kernel pressure at the API gateway and runtime layer.
- Canary/route-weight rebalancing (recent automated shift) amplified concentration of heavy requests on hosts with fragmented GPU memory, triggering NVML resets and subsequent runtime restarts.
- KV cache lock contention during simultaneous prefetches aggravated tail latency and increased hedged retries, amplifying load in a feedback loop.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Support manually paused customer's bulk embedding uploads at 09:32Z (customer cooperated).
- Traffic temporarily shifted off nodes gw-rt-07 and gw-rt-09 via healthcheck weight adjustment at 09:36Z.
- Autoscaler set to immediate scale-up + drain policy to avoid colocating new heavy jobs on warm instances.

Status / next steps:
- Eng SRE oncall (Miguel) currently reproducing failure mode in a scaled staging cluster with a synthetic mix of long-lived streams + large embedding batch uploads.
- Short-term: continue to keep heavy embedding upload policy rate-limited for AtlasHealth.
- Mid-term: evaluate guardrails: per-tenant concurrent-streams cap OR simultaneous-embed-upload threshold; introduce slower prewarm/rehab routing after NVML-resets to avoid immediate traffic reattachment.
- Long-term: investigate kernel fallback behavior and kvcache lock avoidance; consider runtime patch to reduce aggressive prefetch during observed high-conn scenarios.

Customer-facing note:
- Customer informed 09:40Z about active mitigation and recommended to resubmit failed embedding jobs after 2 hours or use smaller batch sizes. Support will follow up with a post-incident summary when investigation completes.

investigation_notes: Healthcheck weights: traffic manager applied automated weight change at 2026-03-14T09:11:32Z — correlates to customer traffic ramp.
Node gw-rt-07 shows GPU memory fragmentation pattern consistent with long lived cache + embedding allocations; NVML resets correlate with fragmentation windows.
Hedged retries doubled during tail-latency spikes, increasing load on worker set by ~28% in peak window.
No immediate evidence of hardware fault — suspect fragmentation + driver stress; vendor driver team engaged if repro confirms deterministic NVML reset.
Potential quick fix: avoid immediate route reattachment to instances that recently reported NVML resets; route-manager should add a cooldown label.
Follow-up created: INT-210203 to track autoscaler/drain policy tuning (internal).
resolution: Mitigations applied (paused customer's heavy uploads; drained affected hosts; temporary rate limits). Root cause investigation ongoing. No permanent fix yet; working on route-manager cooldown and prefetch/backpressure improvements.

Complete staging repro and confirm NVML reset trigger conditions
Define and ship short-term rate-limits/guardrails for dedicated pools (per-tenant concurrency caps)
Create follow-up engineering tickets for kvcache lock improvements and route-manager cooldown behavior
